season.evidence: Logged ascents: Jul 45, Aug 38, Sep 41, Oct 18, Jun 10. Searches (Mountaineers route page, Cascade Climbers/WTA reports, SummitPost) show snow on the High Pass trail and in the summit gully into early July, loose scree through late summer; most ascents Jul-Oct. Stored Jul-Sep confirmed; late June and early October are shoulder months.

track.why: Only one route is catalogued on this peak. 19 Sep 2026 round trip from Twin Lakes Trailhead (start 67 m, end 73 m from our pin) via the High Pass trail, the basin and the south-west spur to the summit (6 m from our pin, 5 m from the surveyed point), returning the same way; matches the stored line. Summited, in season, dense (2770 points).

5 Oct 2025, logged High Pass Trail to south ridge, valid round trip; a month outside the stored window, so second choice.
7 Jul 2025 Southwest Route, summited but the track's start/end are 450 m off our pin and not a clean round trip.

31 Oct 2020 SW chute, outside the window; valid line.

facts.text: Of the two gullies, the left-hand one (marked by a cairn at its top) descends on firmer, slabby rock and was judged safer than the loose main channel; reports from late September and October prefer it for coming down.
In early October the scree is frozen solid at dawn and climbs firmly, but rock released by the thawing sun rattles down the gullies from late morning.
The loose rock is much worse with several parties on the face; choose a weekday in September if you can.

In late June the basin below the south-west spur still holds enough snow to ease the scree, and microspikes were enough without an axe; parking near the lakes may be buried in snow and avalanche debris.
The summit has no false top and a flat, cleared tent-sized spot, but it is very exposed to wind.

notes: Trailhead and summit pins already agree with every recording (within 70 m / 17 m); no pin change. Reports disagree on difficulty (class 2 with choss vs class 3 to 4th-class moves) depending on ridge versus gully line; stored Class 3 is reasonable.
